quote: My younger self did not realize that solving a mystery should make it feel less confusing.
content: The essay’s criterion is not that a solved phenomenon stops being interesting; it is that it stops being mysterious, in the specific sense that the question no longer resists all inquiry. Quantum mechanics is calculable to twelve decimal places, the black-body spectrum is derived rather than wondered at, and the residual strangeness is a dispute about interpretation among people who all agree on every prediction. That is exactly the transformation the essay describes: the mystery moved from the phenomenon to our conceptual apparatus. A theory that lets you compute the answer has made the phenomenon mundane in the only sense the essay uses.

quote: Only then did I realize how reasonable vitalism had seemed at the time
content: Both descriptions are in the sequence because both are true of different moments, and the essay says so: the point of this piece is that vitalism was reasonable from the inside and that its adherents ended by cherishing the gap. That is not a retraction, it is the sequence’s central thesis — mysterious answers do not feel mysterious to the person holding one, which is why a list of contemptible errors is useless unless you also know how they feel from inside. An essay that supplies the inside view of a position an earlier essay judged from outside has completed the argument rather than reversed it.

quote: right up until science finally solved them
content: The induction the essay draws is that mysteries have mechanisms, not that every mystery has been solved. "Life" in the sense at issue — whether there is an élan vital, a substance or force distinguishing living matter — is closed, and biochemistry closed it; the origin of life is a different and open question about a historical pathway, which is a question about what happened rather than about what kind of thing life is. The same distinction applies down the list: the interpretation of quantum mechanics is contested, the formalism is not. Selecting the still-open questions and calling the pattern survivorship works only if the closed ones were not closed.
